description.p: Use one keyboard and mouse across paired computers on your local network. Push the pointer through a screen edge or use a shortcut to switch machines, and take the clipboard with you.

On Wayland, the desktop controls input capture. Beamer can send input out when the pointer crosses an edge, but its shortcut only brings input back. It cannot hold an edge for a full-screen app, keep selected keys on the Linux computer while input is away, or draw crossing effects at the Linux screen edge.

On X11, Beamer can send and receive input across paired computers, including keyboard, pointer and clipboard. The Linux build has been tested on Fedora 44 with GNOME 50 under Wayland; X11 on real hardware and KDE Plasma have not been tested.

description.p: Carries the 1.5.5 audit fixes: Korean Han/Yeong and Hanja key repeat on X11, typed machine names on US-English systems, the Crossing shortcut tile subtitle, and the single-display map frame.
Adds layout profiles, shake to come home, resizable machine tiles on the Crossing map, and an Italian translation.
Fixes the shortcut leaving input stranded when it picked a machine that had just turned it away.
Adds pointer hiding on idle screens, idle takeover, per-screen crossing with contact-span matching, and Mac and Qt refresh improvements.
Adds the shared desk map, granular settings, dormant pairing repair and Linux crossing effects.
Fixes the Linux key-box hint and other issues found in the 1.5.0 release.
Adds Linux support and expands multi-computer support.
